item.title: Heartbreak for India as Oz advance to semis after goalless Hockey WC draw
item.description: Indian women’s Hockey World Cup campaign ended after Australia held them to a 0-0 draw and advanced to the semifinals on goals scored. Australia had two goals ruled out after reviews, while India missed key chances and penalty corners. Despite a strong second-half push and removing their goalkeeper late on, India could not find the winner and will now play for fifth place.

item.title: What makes September 3 important for international students in the US on F and J visas
item.description: A federal court is scheduled to review arguments on September 3, 2026, concerning a newly proposed rule that overhauls the current 'duration of status' policy which impacts international students. The plaintiffs contend that this alteration fosters ambiguity and adversely affects educational institutions. They reference economic repercussions and dismiss comments from DHS.

item.title: Microsoft has a 6-word answer for students wondering if coding is still worth it
item.description: Microsoft Learn has told students on X that learning to code is worth it "now more than ever", even as AI writes a growing share of software. Satya Nadella says AI already produces up to 30% of Microsoft's code, while Google puts its figure at 75%. The skill has not died, it has shifted from writing syntax to reviewing, debugging and directing AI-generated code.

item.title: Apollo 15 brought back green glass beads; decades later they revealed lunar water
item.description: Apollo 15 astronauts found unusual green flecks on the Moon's surface. These flecks were later identified as volcanic glass beads containing trapped water. Researchers discovered hydrogen within these tiny beads, proving lunar water existed. This finding challenged the long-held belief that the Moon was extremely dry. The discovery revealed significant water presence deep within the Moon's interior.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: New Zealand wiped out 200,000 mice on Antipodes Island, boosting native birds
item.description: New Zealand's 2016 effort to remove an estimated 200,000 mice from Antipodes Island has been followed by a clear recovery in native bird populations. Monitoring confirmed the mice were gone in 2018, while surveys over the next six years found Antipodes Island pipit and snipe numbers had more than doubled.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Why ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt is 'unhappy' with his former boss Sergey Brin
item.description: Eric Schmidt has expressed discontent regarding Sergey Brin's financial backing for political measures, which includes a staggering $100 million aimed at challenging California's Proposition 40. His irritation is exacerbated by investments in various ballot initiatives, particularly a wealth tax that impacts individuals boasting a net worth exceeding $1 billion. The former Google CEO is determined to thwart this proposed tax targeting billionaires.

item.title: Doctor assaulted by patient’s son inside Maharashtra hospital, FIR registered
item.description: An orthopaedic surgeon was assaulted by a patient's son at a private hospital late Saturday night, raising concerns among other patients present. This incident mirrors a previous attack on medical professionals by a local corporator just weeks prior. Authorities have filed a First Information Report (FIR) and are actively investigating this latest attack; the suspect from the prior incident is currently in Goa.

item.title: How Travis Kelce built $90 million fortune as podcast deal reshaped his wealth
item.description: Travis Kelce's net worth reaches ninety million dollars by 2026. His NFL salary totals over one hundred eleven million dollars in career earnings. A significant podcast deal with Amazon's Wondery is valued at one hundred million dollars. Endorsement income and business ventures further boost his substantial financial portfolio. His marriage to Taylor Swift has also broadened his commercial appeal.

item.title: Charlotte Flair vs Alexa Bliss net worth 2026: Who is richer among WWE stars?
item.description: Alexa Bliss and Charlotte Flair have earned a lot of money through WWE contracts, championships, merchandise, endorsements and media work. Flair is generally accepted to be wealthier, although Bliss has built up a strong commercial profile for herself. Both performers have not released complete financial records, so all of the net worth figures are estimates.

item.title: Tom Brady’s son Jack chooses basketball over football as breakout turns heads
item.description: Tom Brady’s eldest son, Jack Moynahan, is attracting attention for his rising basketball career rather than following his father into football. The 6-foot-6 athlete recently showcased his skills at The Newman School in Boston, prompting enthusiastic reactions from fans. His mother, Bridget Moynahan, previously said Jack was more interested in basketball and lacrosse. Now, his growing presence on the court suggests he is carving out a sporting identity of his own.

item.title: Asim Riaz denies ex-GF Himanshi Khurana’s Islam conversion allegation
item.description: Asim Riaz has firmly dismissed Himanshi Khurana's allegations regarding religious conversion during their previous romance, labeling such claims as childish. He clarified that he never pressured anyone to alter their faith. Himanshi recounted how Asim highlighted positive aspects of his religion, yet she felt that converting would betray her own beliefs. The couple, who first connected on Bigg Boss 13, ended their relationship in 2023.

item.title: Trump tariffs: What India can learn from Canada’s failed trade talks with US
item.description: Ottawa said it would introduce “dollar-for-dollar” retaliatory tariffs from September 8. The move brought an end to talks that had started on February 1, 2025, after the first round of new US tariffs was imposed.
item.dc:creator: SMRITI JAIN

item.title: From roses to stone and statues: Trump's makeover of White House Rose Garden
item.description: President Trump is making significant renovations to the White House grounds, highlighted by the addition of new statues in the Rose Garden. Among these is a bronze statue of Thomas Jefferson, placed alongside other notable American figures. This revitalization effort aims to modernize the historic garden while ensuring the preservation of the White House complex for future generations.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: Rest, viral and not in India's XI for Colombo Test: Mysterious case of Kuldeep
item.description: Conflicting explanations from the Indian camp have added intrigue to Kuldeep Yadav's absence from the Colombo Test, with the chinaman missing out as India handed Saransh Jain a debut. Kuldeep did travel with the team and was also spotted in the dugout alongside Sarfaraz Khan. The official word from the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) remains "viral illness".

item.title: Meet Sir Nils Olav III, world's highest-ranking penguin, set to become a father
item.description: The world’s highest-ranking penguin, Major General Sir Nils Olav III, is set to become a father after his partner Connie laid an egg at Edinburgh Zoo. The surprise arrival marks the zoo’s first king penguin egg in 17 years. Keepers are closely monitoring the inexperienced parents as they take turns protecting and warming the egg.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: ‘They may have fled to Odisha’: Mystery deepens in Tamil Nadu Express murder case
item.description: Chennai police are searching Odisha for a couple suspected in a brutal murder case. Severed body parts of Hayathun Nisha were found in a suitcase aboard a train. Investigators recovered more remains from the suspects' rented Chennai residence. The couple is believed to have fled to Odisha after the discovery. Authorities are working to determine the motive behind the gruesome killing.
item.dc:creator: DEBABRATA MOHAPATRA

item.title: Woman kills husband in brutal knife attack in Haryana, later jumps from rooftop
item.description: In a shocking incident on Saturday, a woman reportedly murdered her husband in Kurukshetra using knives. Rajesh, a water supplier, suffered life-threatening abdominal injuries, including an open abdomen with protruding intestines. A post-mortem examination uncovered missing sections of his liver and right kidney. The couple had been residing together in Kurukshetra for approximately one year.
item.dc:creator: JASKARAN SINGH

item.title: Yashasvi Jaiswal fight: 'Shouldn't have gone so close,' says India batting coach
item.description: Yashasvi Jaiswal charged toward the bowler, making visible contact with Fernando's head. The Sri Lankan players stepped in, separated the two and prevented the situation from escalating. India's batting coach Sitanshu Kotak felt Jaiswal shouldn't have gone so close and termed the incident as something that happened in the "heat of the moment".
item.dc:creator: SAHIL MALHOTRA

item.title: How Ananta Maharaj row exposed old fault lines over Netaji
item.description: Recent remarks questioned Netaji's freedom struggle contributions and the Indian National Army's achievements. Historical records and Nehru's statements contradict claims of him being a 'war criminal'. Bose's political journey involved disagreements with Congress and alliances for independence. Various political groups now claim facets of Netaji's ideology and nationalism. Debates continue over his death and the preservation of his legacy.
item.dc:creator: ARGHYA PRASUN ROYCHOWDHURY

item.description: BAI secretary general Sanjay Mishra said the Super 750 event, scheduled for the last week of January 2028, would clash with heightened security protocols in the national capital around January 26.

item.title: 21 ex-captains, including Gavaskar, Kapil, renew appeal for Imran Khan's treatment
item.description: In February this year, 14 legendary captains from five countries — including Gavaskar, Kapil Dev and Greg Chappell, a former head coach of Team India — had made a fervent, emotional appeal to the Pakistan government about ensuring proper treatment for Imran, amid mounting concerns about the cricketing icon’s health. However, there was no response from the Pakistan government to the cricket legends’ request.

item.title: Anti-reservation protest: Several detained as crowd gathers at Delhi's Connaught Place
item.description: Around 300 individuals protested caste-based reservation in Delhi's Connaught Place, advocating for economic criteria over caste for government support and reforms in the quota system. Police detained over 20 protesters for demonstrating without permission. The "Reservation Hatao Andolan" organized the event, emphasizing that reforms should ensure benefits reach the truly needy across all communities.
item.dc:creator: PRACHI KUMAWAT

item.title: Destroyed in Op Sindoor, JeM's terror base operational again; Pak govt gave Rs 8 cr
item.description: Fresh footage indicates it is fully operational again, complete with reconstructed domes, updated interior plastering, new paint, and premium marble flooring that conceals previous blast damage. Deep blast zones within the primary hall were filled with concrete, while ruined satellite buildings—including the Al-Sabir seminary and housing units for leadership—were demolished to enable new construction.
item.dc:creator: RAJ SHEKHAR JHA

item.title: KPSC exam scam: ED raids 'missing' IAS officer's premises in Bengaluru, Bareilly
item.description: In a significant move, the Enforcement Directorate raided the properties of IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar located in Bengaluru and Bareilly. This action is tied to a money laundering case concerning malpractice in KPSC examinations, particularly focusing on a veterinary officer recruitment scandal. Gangwar's past role as the KPSC Controller of Examinations adds weight to the inquiry, following prior searches involving KPSC facilities and former officials.
item.dc:creator: PRACHI KUMAWAT

item.title: IND vs SL: Devdutt Padikkal, Shubman Gill and the trailer of a blockbuster
item.description: Devdutt Padikkal scored his second Test hundred, but it was his 120-run stand with India captain Shubman Gill that offered a trailer of a potential blockbuster in the making. India's No. 3 and No. 4 have only had three century partnerships since 2019, and this third instance in Colombo today is certainly not going to be the first and last involving the left-right pair.
item.dc:creator: SAHIL MALHOTRA

item.title: Hindu family of four found dead in locked home in Bangladesh; strangulation suspected
item.description: A chilling scene unfolded when police discovered the bodies of four members of a Hindu family in their locked home. Initial investigations point to strangulation and a possible robbery. The family's absence since Thursday and the lack of phone activity raised alarm. Following a forced entry, officers located the victims throughout the house. Autopsy results are pending to establish the precise cause of their untimely deaths.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: Two 50s, 7 wickets: How Stokes fared on his red-ball return after retirement
item.description: Ben Stokes made a stunning return to red-ball cricket, scoring 53 and an unbeaten 66 before taking seven wickets against Derbyshire. His 5-17 spell included three wickets in four balls, helping Durham secure a massive 338-run victory. The win moved Durham to the top of the County Championship, with Stokes showing he remains a major all-round force.

item.title: 'There won't be a teleprompter': Raut dares PM Modi, Shah to sing full Vande Mataram
item.description: Sanjay Raut challenged Prime Minister Modi and Amit Shah to sing Vande Mataram without teleprompters. He also questioned the government's economic record and rising inflation. The BJP condemned the Congress decision to sing only two stanzas of the national song. Congress leaders accused the BJP of politicizing patriotism and nationalism for political gain. Both parties are trading charges over the national song's recitation and its significance.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA
